title: Researchers Use Chemical Examinations and Human Smell to Study Ancient Remains
speaker: VOA Learning English

sentences.en: A recent study about the smell of Egyptian mummies reached some surprising findings.
sentences.zh: 最近一项有关埃及木乃伊的味道的研究得出了一些令人吃惊的结论。

sentences.en: The ancient bodies did not smell bad, the researchers found.
sentences.zh: 古老的身体没有臭味, 研究人员发现了。

sentences.en: Instead, they say, the remains mostly smelled good.
sentences.zh: 相反,他们说,遗体的味道大多良好。

sentences.en: Cecilia Bembibre is director of research at University College London's Institute for Sustainable Heritage. “In films and books, terrible things happen to those who smell mummified bodies,” she said. “We were surprised at the pleasantness of them."
sentences.zh: Cecilia Bembibre是伦敦大学可持续遗产研究所的研究主任。 她说 : “ 在电影和书籍中,那些闻到木乃伊尸体的人会遭遇可怕的事情。 ”她说 : “ 我们感到惊讶的是,他们很愉快。 ”

sentences.en: The researchers reported the leading descriptions of the smells as “woody,” “spicy” and “sweet.” They also reported a floral or flowery smell.
sentences.zh: 研究者们报告了关于这种气味的主要描述,称之为“木质 ” 、 “辣” 和“甜味 ” 。 他们还报告了一种花卉或花朵的气味。

sentences.en: That smell could be from pine and juniper resins used in mummification; a process designed to protect the body from decay.
sentences.zh: 这种气味可能来自木乃伊中使用的松树和柔性树脂;这是一种保护身体不腐烂的过程。

sentences.en: The study appeared recently in the Journal of the American Chemical Society.
sentences.zh: 这项研究最近载于《美国化学协会杂志》。

sentences.en: It used both chemical examinations and several human smellers to study nine mummies.
sentences.zh: 它使用化学检查和几个人嗅觉来研究9个木乃伊。

sentences.en: The mummies, some around 5,000 years old, had been housed at the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.
sentences.zh: 大约5 000岁的木乃伊人被安置在开罗的埃及博物馆。

sentences.en: Bembibre, one of the report’s writers, said the researchers wanted to study the smell of mummies because it has long been a subject of interest for the public and researchers alike.
sentences.zh: 报告作者之一Bembibre表示, 研究人员想研究木乃伊的味道,

sentences.en: She added that even fiction writers have written pages of work on the subject — for good reason.
sentences.zh: 她补充说,甚至连小说作家都写了有关这一主题的著作页——这是有正当理由的。

sentences.en: Scent, or smell, was an important consideration in the mummification process.
sentences.zh: 气味或气味是木乃伊过程的一个重要考虑因素。

sentences.en: This process used oils and plant-based materials to protect the body and its spirit for the afterlife.
sentences.zh: 这一过程利用油料和植物材料来保护身体及其后世精神。

sentences.en: Mummification was largely used for powerful people such as pharaohs and other leaders.
sentences.zh: 穆斯林化主要用于法老和其他领导人等有势力的人。

sentences.en: Pleasant smells were linked with purity and gods.
sentences.zh: 欢乐的气味与纯洁和上帝联系在一起。

sentences.en: Bad smells were signs of corruption and decay.
sentences.zh: 坏的气味是腐败和腐烂的迹象。

sentences.en: Researchers did not want to directly measure the mummies, because doing so might be damaging.
sentences.zh: 研究人员不想直接测量木乃伊,因为这样做可能会造成损害。

sentences.en: Instead, researchers were able to take measurements that did not involve touching the mummies.
sentences.zh: 相反,研究人员能够进行不涉及触摸木乃伊的测量。

sentences.en: Researchers from UCL and the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia were able to measure smells, pesticides, and other effects due to mold, bacteria or microorganisms.
sentences.zh: 斯洛文尼亚联合劳工局和卢布尔雅那大学的研究人员能够测量气味、农药以及霉菌、细菌或微生物造成的其他影响。

sentences.en: Using technical instruments to measure air molecules released from sarcophagi was very important, said Matija Strlič, a chemistry professor at the University of Ljubljana.
sentences.zh: 卢布尔雅那大学的化学教授Matija Strlič说,使用技术仪器测量从石棺中释放的空气分子非常重要。

sentences.en: "It tells us potentially what social class a mummy was from and therefore reveals a lot of information about the mummified body...." he said. “We believe that this approach is potentially of huge interest to other types of museum collections.”
sentences.zh: “它告诉我们一个木乃伊来自什么社会阶层,

sentences.en: Barbara Huber of the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology in Germany was not involved in the study.
sentences.zh: 德国马克斯·普朗克地质人类学研究所的Barbara Huber没有参与这项研究。

sentences.en: Huber said the findings provide important data on compounds that could preserve or damage mummified remains.
sentences.zh: Huber说,调查结果提供了关于可保存或损坏木质遗骸的化合物的重要数据。

sentences.en: The information could be used to better protect the ancient bodies for future generations.
sentences.zh: 这些信息可用于更好地保护古老的身体,供后代使用。

sentences.en: Huber said that over thousands of years, differing conditions have changed the scents of the mummies in a major way.
sentences.zh: Huber说,几千年来, 不同的条件 已经改变了木乃伊的气味 在一个主要的方式。

sentences.en: Huber wrote a study two years ago that examined a jar that had contained mummified organs of a woman.
sentences.zh: Huber两年前写了一篇研究 检查了一个罐子 里面装着一个女人的木乃伊器官

sentences.en: The goal was to identify the material used to preserve the organs and what that would show about ancient trade paths.
sentences.zh: 目的是查明用于保存器官的材料以及古代贸易路径将显示什么。

sentences.en: Researchers of the current study hope to do something similar.
sentences.zh: 目前研究的研究人员希望做类似的事情。

sentences.en: They want to use their findings to develop “smellscapes” to recreate the scents they discovered.
sentences.zh: 他们想利用他们的调查结果来开发“模版”,以重新创造他们发现的气味。

sentences.en: They also want to change the experience for future museumgoers.
sentences.zh: 他们还想为未来的博物馆馆员改变经验。

sentences.en: Bembibre said museums generally ask visitors to experience everything with their eyes.
sentences.zh: Bembibre说,博物馆通常要求参观者用眼睛体验一切。

sentences.en: She added that seeing mummies through “a glass case reduces the experience because we don’t get to smell them.” Smelling the scents of mummification would improve the museum visitors’ experiences, she suggested, as smell is one of the ways that people understand the world.
sentences.zh: 她补充说,通过“玻璃箱”看到木乃伊会减少经验,因为我们无法闻到它们。 她建议,嗅到木乃伊的气味会改善博物馆参观者的经历,因为气味是人们了解世界的方式之一。

sentences.en: I’m John Russell. Brian Melley reported on this story for the Associated Press.
sentences.zh: 我是John Russell。Brian Melley为美联社报导了这个故事。

sentences.en: John Russell adapted it for VOA Learning English.
sentences.zh: John Russell改编了它 用于VOA学习英语。
